questions.q: What does pd.read_csv() do compared to Lesson 20's manual file loop?
options: Opens the file, parses every row, infers every column's type, and hands back a ready-to-use DataFrame, all in one line
It only opens the file without reading any content
It requires exactly the same amount of manual code as Lesson 20
It only works on files smaller than 1KB
questions.explain: This single function call replaces the entire manual open/loop/split/convert process.

questions.q: What does the parse_dates parameter do?
options: Converts specified columns into a real datetime type instead of loading them as plain text
Deletes any column containing a date
Automatically sorts the DataFrame by date
Only works on JSON files, never CSV
questions.explain: Without it, a date column loads as text and can't be filtered by year, month, or day directly.

questions.q: What does the dtype parameter do in read_csv()?
options: Overrides Pandas' automatic type inference for a specific column
Deletes a column from the resulting DataFrame
Only applies to numeric columns
Converts the entire file to a different file format
questions.explain: This is useful for a column like VendorID that looks numeric but should be kept as text.

questions.q: Why does getting a column's type wrong at read time cause problems later?
options: A date stored as text can't be filtered by year, and a numeric-looking ID stored as a number might lose meaningful leading characters
It has no real consequences at all
Pandas automatically fixes type errors after the fact
Wrong types only affect how a DataFrame prints, never its actual behavior
questions.explain: Catching this deliberately at read_csv() time avoids debugging subtle issues several lessons later.

questions.q: What shape of JSON does pd.read_json() convert most directly into a DataFrame?
options: A list of objects — the same shape as Lesson 15's list of dictionaries
Only a single JSON object with no list at all
JSON cannot be read into a DataFrame under any circumstances
Only deeply nested JSON with no flat records
questions.explain: This is exactly the shape read_json() handles the same way read_csv() handles a CSV's rows.
